newsitem.title: USA: James River, Fort Howard to merge - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: James River, Fort Howard to merge - WSJ.

text.p: James River Corp has agreed to merger with Fort Howard Corp in a stock swap valued at about $3.4 billion or $42.45 a share for Fort Howard shareholders, plus the assumption of debt, the Wall Street Journal said in Monday's electronic edition.
According to people familiar with the situation, the boards of the two companies approved the deal on Sunday and the agreement was expected to be announced today, the newspaper said.
The Journal said the new company, which would be called Fort James Corp, would be a giant tissue and paper goods firm with annual revenues of more than $7 billion.
Neither company was immediately available to comment on the report.
The total debt and equity of Fort Howard was valued at about $5.8 billion, including about $2.4 billion in debt for Fort Howard, left over from its 1980s leveraged buyout, the newspaper said.
Ford Howard shareholders would receive 1.375 shares of James River per Fort Howard share held, the paper said.
The transaction was expected to be accretive to earnings by the end of 1997, boosting earnings 10 percent in 1998 because of $150 million in cost savings in the first full year, the Journal said.
According to people familiar with the situation, James River Chairman and Chief Executive Miles Marsh would be chairman and CEO of the new company, the Journal said.
Fort Howard Chairman and CEO Michael Riordan would become president and chief operating officer of the new company, the paper said.
James River shares closed up 7/8 at 30-7/8 on Friday while closed up 1/2 at 36-1/2.
